land.text: Urundi, the southern half of the Belgian-administered Ruanda-Urundi: 'Part of Ruanda-Urundi: 1916–1962'

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws Ruanda-Urundi inside its Belgian Congo shape; the belgian-congo dossier carries the 1 July 1962 loss. The older Kingdom of Burundi (kingdom-of-burundi, to 1903) is the same land before the German and Belgian colonial period.

capitals.name: Bujumbura
capitals.note: 'The colonial capital Usumbura was officially renamed Bujumbura at independence in 1962.' It stays the economic capital after 2019.

capitals.name: Gitega (political capital)
capitals.note: Infobox: 'Gitega (political)' and 'Bujumbura (economic)'. The page body gives no date; 2019 comes from the title of a cited law, 'Loi n°1/04 du 04 février 2019 portant Fixation de la Capitale Politique et de la Capitale Economique du Burundi'.

correction.text: Burundi as it stands in Cliopatria's 1963 shape, applied from independence: 'The country claimed independence on 1 July 1962' as a constitutional monarchy under Mwami Mwambutsa IV

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Republic of Burundi begins in 1963 but independence was 1 July 1962 (infobox 'Independence from Belgium: 1 July 1962'). The land is the 1963 shape unchanged; the page reports no border change since 1962. Until 28 November 1966 the state was a kingdom, not a republic.

24,740 km2 against the infobox 27,834 km2 total (10 percent water, about 25,050 km2 of land): ratio 0.89 of the total, 0.99 of the land. The page reports no border changes or disputes with Rwanda, Tanzania or the DR Congo since 1962, so one shape holds for 1963-2023. Cliopatria labels the whole row 'Republic'; the republic dates from 28 November 1966 (rename event).
Same outline and area (24,740 km2) as 1963-2023; nothing on the page changes the territory in 2024.

region.text: Burundi: 'The country claimed independence on 1 July 1962'; infobox 'Part of Ruanda-Urundi: 1916–1962'

ledger.note: 1 July 1962: Burundi becomes independent of Belgium as a kingdom under Mwami Mwambutsa IV. 'Burundi gained independence in 1962 and initially retained the monarchy'; the state 'legally changed its name from Ruanda-Urundi to Burundi'. The page names the country, not a boundary.

28 November 1966: Prime Minister Micombero deposes Ntare V and abolishes the monarchy; Burundi becomes a republic. 'Prime Minister Micombero carried out another coup, this time deposing Ntare, abolishing the monarchy'; infobox 'Republic: 28 November 1966'. Same state and land, so the colour continues (rule 2).

2019: the political capital moves from Bujumbura to Gitega; Bujumbura stays the economic capital. The page body gives no date: the infobox lists 'Gitega (political)' and 'Bujumbura (economic)', and the year is that of the cited law of 4 February 2019.

wars.name: Burundian Civil War
wars.outcome: The infobox dates it '21 October 1993 – 15 May 2005'; the page describes 'persistent violence between Hutu rebels and the Tutsi majority army'. It reports no change of border.
wars.note: No rebel-held zone is dated on the page, so none is mapped (rule 5 needs a land and a date).

wars.name: Second Congo War
wars.outcome: The page lists Burundi among the foreign state actors (Uganda, Rwanda, Burundi) and says 'Burundi also retaliated, occupying a portion of northeastern Congo'; the war 'officially ended on 18 July 2003'.
wars.note: The page gives Burundi's occupation neither a date nor a boundary (and 'northeastern' is odd for a country on Congo's eastern edge), so it is not mapped as an occupation event; the DR Congo dossier should settle it.

certainty.note: Inherited colonial-era boundaries (Ruanda-Urundi split 'along traditional lines' in 1962); the page records no change or dispute since. The Lake Tanganyika shoreline in the south-west is a natural line.

sources.title: Burundi

sources.title: Second Congo War
sources.note: Burundi's role in the Second Congo War (one sentence, no dates or boundary).

notes: Cliopatria's single Burundi shape is the modern country for 1963-2023 and 2024; the page records no border change since independence, so the dossier adds only the 1962 start (new keyframe), the 1966 kingdom-to-republic rename and the 2019 move of the political capital. No ruler strip: the page gives no list of heads of state, and the ruler list was not opened within the 1-2 page budget. Page conflict: the body says Burundi became part of German East Africa in 1885, the infobox 1890 (not needed here). The Second Congo War sentence on Burundi is the only page evidence of a Burundian occupation of Congolese land and carries no date; see the DR Congo dossier. First Congo War (1996-97) not opened (page budget).
